verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              ततोऽहं निशि राजेन्द्र प्रणम्य शिरसा तदा। ब्राह्मणानां पितॄणां च देवतानां च सर्वशः ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Then during the night, 0 great king, having bowed to all the Brahmanas, my fore fathers, all the gods,

verses.sanskrit: नक्तंचराणां भूतानां राजन्यानां विशाम्पते। शयनं प्राप्य रहिते मनसा समचिन्तयम् ॥२॥
verses.english: To all those beings that walk about in the night, to all elements, earth, water, fir, air and the sky, and to all kings, O lord of earth, I lay down on my bed, and being all alone, I began to reflect (thus).

verses.sanskrit: जामदग्न्येन मे युद्धमिदं परमदारुणम्। अहानि च बहून्यद्य वर्तते सुमहात्ययम् ॥३॥
verses.english: This terrible battle, between myself and Jamadgnya, being as it is of high and mighty consequence, lasted for many a day.

verses.sanskrit: न च रामं महावीरर्यं शक्नोमि रणमूर्धनि। विजेतुं समरे विप्रं जामदग्न्यं महाबलम् ॥४॥
verses.english: And yet I have not been able to vanquish, in fight on the field of battle, this twice-born Rama, known as Jamadgnya who is of great might and energy.

verses.sanskrit: यदि शक्यो मया जेतुं जामदग्न्यः प्रतापवान्। दैवतानि प्रसन्नानि दर्शयन्तु निशां मम ॥५॥
verses.english: I indeed, it lies in my power to vanquish this powerful son of Jamadagni, let the gods, well-pleased, show themselves to me during the night.

verses.sanskrit: ततो निशि च राजेन्द्र प्रसुप्तः शरविक्षतः। दक्षिणेनेह पार्श्वेन प्रभातसमये तदा ॥६॥
verses.english: Then, O great king, mangled with arrows, as I lay asleep that night on my right, at about dawn came,

verses.sanskrit: ततोऽहं विप्रमुख्यैस्तैर्यैरस्मि पतितो रथात्। उत्थापितो धृतश्चैव मा भैरिति च सान्त्वितः ॥७॥
verses.english: Those foremost of Brahmanas by whom I had been raised up when I had fallen down from chariot, and who had held me and comforted me, saying, “Fear not.”

verses.sanskrit: त एव मां महाराज स्वप्नदर्शनमेत्य वै। परिवार्याब्रुवन् वाक्यं तन्निबोध कुरुद्धह ॥८॥
verses.english: Even they, O great king, showing themselves to me (during my sleep) in a dream, stood around me, and spoke these words; Hear them, O perpetuator of Kuru's race,

verses.sanskrit: उत्तिष्ठ मा भैर्गाङ्गेय न भयं तेऽस्ति किञ्चन। रक्षामहे त्वां कौरव्य स्वशरीरं हि नो भवान् ॥९॥
verses.english: Rise up and do not fear, O son of Ganga, you have not the least fear, for we will protect you, O son, who are own body.

verses.sanskrit: न त्वां रामो रणे जेता जामदग्न्यः कथञ्चन। त्वमेव समरे रामं विजेता भरतर्षभ ॥१०॥
verses.english: Rama, the son of Jamadagni, by no means will vanquish you in battle. (Rather), you will vanquish Rama in battle, O best of Bharata's race.

verses.sanskrit: इदमस्रं सुदयितं प्रत्यभिज्ञास्यते भवान्। विदितं हि तवाप्येतत् पूर्वस्मिन् देहधारणे ॥११॥
verses.english: This well-beloved weapon you will recognize for it was known to you in your previous birth.

verses.sanskrit: प्राजापत्यं विश्वकृतं प्रस्वापं नाम भारत। नहीदं वेद रामोऽपि पृथिव्यां वा पुमान् क्वचित्॥१२॥
verses.english: It appertains to the lord of all creatures (Brahma) and was manufactured by the divine architect; it is named Prasvapa, O Bharata. It is not known even to Rama nor to any body else on the earth.

verses.sanskrit: तत् स्मरस्व महाबाहो भृशं संयोजयस्व च। उपस्थास्यति राजेन्द्र स्वयमेव तवानघ ॥१३॥
verses.english: Recollect it therefore, O you of mighty arms, and apply it steadily and with all your strength. It will come to you of itself, O you great king and sinless one.

verses.sanskrit: येन सर्वान् महावीर्यान् प्रशासिष्यसि कौरव। न च रामः क्षयं गन्ता तेनास्त्रेण नराधिप ॥१४॥
verses.english: By this weapon, by which O son of Kuru, you will hold in check all persons of mighty energy, Rama will not be killed outright, O king of men.

verses.sanskrit: एनसा न तु संयोगं प्राप्स्यसे जातु मानद। स्वप्स्यते जामदग्न्योऽसौ त्वद्बाणबलपीडितः ॥१५॥
verses.english: No crime will therefore attach to you o giver of honors. And this son of Jamadagni will fall asleep, afflicted by the might of this weapon of yours.

verses.sanskrit: ततो जित्वा त्वमेवैनं पुनरुत्थापयिष्यसि। अस्त्रेण दयितेनाजौ भीष्म संबोधनेन वै ॥१६॥
verses.english: Having thus vanquished him, you yourself will raise him up again to the battle-field by that dear weapon, O Bhishma, known as Samabodhana.

verses.sanskrit: एवं कुरुष्व कौरव्य प्रभाते रथमास्थितः। प्रसुप्तं वा मृतं वेति तुल्यं मन्यामहे वयम् ॥१७॥
verses.english: Do as we tell you, O son of Kuru, seated on your chariot at day-break. Asleep or dead, We consider it to be the same.

verses.sanskrit: न च रामेण मर्तव्यं कदाचिदपि पार्थिव। ततः समुत्पन्नमिदं प्रस्वापं युज्यतामिति ॥१८॥
verses.english: O king, Rama will not die by any means. Apply therefore, this (weapon) Prasvapa, happily brought for you.

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्त्वाऽन्तर्हिता राजन् सर्व एव द्विजोत्तमाः। अष्टौ सदृशरूपास्ते सर्वे भासुरमूर्तयः ॥१९॥
verses.english: Having said this all those best of Brahmanas vanished, O king. They were eight in number, resembling one another in appearance, and shone brightly, having no material bodies.
